After reviewing the information, we determined that the owner had a debit/credit card replaced after it was stolen but continued using older checks that did not match the current account information. This created confusion and resulted in ACH processing issues. We worked through the details and expect to have a corrected ACH form submitted shortly with the proper banking information. Once the updated information is received and processed, funding should be directed to the correct account and the issue should be resolved.

This ensures financing is presented to all customers as part of their standard process. While adoption may be limited due to the area’s customer demographics and lower financing demand, it was encouraging to see EasyPay incorporated into their customer communication process.

Spoke with Sabrina, the manager. After several months of follow-up visits encouraging the shop to use EasyPay again, they are finally back on board and are now running EasyPay first. They are once again producing the same level of business they did with us when we were RIC, which is a great win.

This is a good example of how consistent relationship-building and periodic follow-up can help re-engage inactive merchants over time.

Sabrina shared that overall business has been slower, but higher repair costs have resulted in larger average ticket sizes, helping offset the decrease in car count. Based on their current activity, I estimate they have the potential to fund approximately $8K–$10K with EasyPay each month.

The shop is currently on a $20 spiff. Sabrina requested a poster, which I will provide once they are back in stock. I reminded her to reach out to Connor or me if she needs any assistance.

He explained that he only uses KOALAFI when EasyPay does not approve enough to cover the full repair.

Tre mentioned that he has had some issues in the past regarding sales tax on invoices. Connor previously reviewed the proper procedures with him. He asked me how the tax exemption works and whether the shop could get in trouble for not charging sales tax. I showed him the Georgia reseller tax ID number located in his Business Center and advised him to have the owner provide that number to their tax professional, who would know how to handle it appropriately.

Tre had no other questions or concerns. I left behind a few EasyPay pens and notepads and reminded him to reach out to Connor or me if he ever needs assistance.

Called and spoke with Robert. Our conversation focused primarily on the recent application declines he has been experiencing. He shared that **EasyPay is the only financing option** they offer, so when customers are declined, they often have no alternative way to finance their repairs.

Robert provided two recent examples that have been frustrating for both him and his customers. One customer had previously completed a lease with EasyPay but was declined when applying again. Another customer was initially approved, but after the approval expired and they reapplied, the second application was denied.

Robert expressed frustration with these situations because EasyPay is their only financing solution for customers who cannot pay the full repair cost upfront. I acknowledged his concerns, thanked him for the feedback, and encouraged him to continue reaching out whenever he encounters situations where we may be able to assist.

Spoke with Catherine. She shared that the shop has been struggling over the past couple of months. Ever since ICE activity increased in Houston, they’ve seen a significant decline in business because many of their customers work in landscaping, roofing, construction, and other trades that rely on work trucks. She explained that many workers have been detained or are no longer working, so those trucks are not being used and therefore don’t need repairs.

She is hopeful that business will improve once school starts, as families may need to repair additional vehicles for their children or prepare their cars for the new school year. For now, the shop is simply waiting for business to pick back up.

Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
I spoke with Joe. He said everything is going well, but they haven’t had much need for financing lately.

The shop doesn’t have a dedicated front desk employee. The mechanics handle both the repairs and customer interactions, so they’re constantly moving between the shop and the office. Because of that, there’s no one specifically responsible for offering financing, and it often gets overlooked unless a customer asks about it. This has limited the number of EasyPay applications submitted.

Sam's main concern was the policy regarding partial transactions. I explained that the EasyPay lease must cover the full invoice amount. Sam suggested that a broader retraining may be beneficial, as he believes other Christian Brothers locations may be following the same process. He became frustrated during the conversation and explained that he has been running the business this way for the past 10 years. Full Comments:
I spoke with Shanon, who informed me that Johnny is the primary point of contact for Easy Pay and Dave is the owner. He mentioned that they work with several financing providers, including American First Finance, Affirm, SNAP, Synchrony, and Sunbit.

According to Canon, all financing options are presented to the customer, and the customer ultimately decides which provider to use. He noted that approval outcomes vary by lender. In some cases, customers are approved through Easy Pay when other providers decline them, while in other situations, customers who are not approved through Easy Pay are able to obtain financing through another provider, most commonly SNAP.

I also confirmed their hours of operation and gathered additional shop details. The business operates 14 service bays and has an average repair order (ARO) of approximately $1,000.

Subject: 00UTO00000e2c3l2AA
Full Comments:
I spoke with Dan, the owner. They have had a wonderful July and August. He said these are his biggest months because people are purchasing phones, computers, and tablets for back-to-school.

Dan said he would be doing even more business with us if he received more approvals, but he understands that people’s credit has been challenging in the current economy. His only callout was that he wishes we had higher approval amounts and could go beyond our $5,000 limit. I explained that we occasionally approve up to $6,000, but that is rare and typically only occurs with customers who have extremely strong credit.

He did not have any other callouts or questions. I noticed he was running low on marketing materials, so I ordered more for the store. I also told him to reach out to Connor or me if he needed any assistance.

Subject: 00TTO000011tg412AA
Full Comments:
Spoke with Michelle. She shared that business is still somewhat slow, but the shop is gradually starting to pick up, so she is hopeful this will lead to an increase in applications and overall numbers.

We reviewed their activity for the month and noted that they have had one application approved for $5,000, with only $1,300 currently used. I reminded her that if the customer needs additional funds within the 30-day approval period, they can submit a new application and utilize the remaining available balance. After the 30-day period expires, the unused balance is no longer available, and the customer would need to submit a new application and go through the pre-approval process again.

Michelle stated that she did not need additional training, but appreciated the refresher and reminders provided during the call. I also made her aware of the training videos available directly through the portal. She had no major concerns or complaints at this time.

Follow up notes for ISR: Monroe will monitor the location and return in 2 weeks to see if applications improve.

I advised her that if they begin working with insurance claims, EasyPay can be used to help customers cover their deductibles.

We also reviewed the 90-day payment option to ensure she is comfortable presenting it to customers and providing them with the appropriate information so they can evaluate all available payment options.

We also reviewed the available early purchase options and discussed how they work so he can accurately explain them to customers and answer any related questions.

July was his worst month of the year for both his repair and detailing businesses\. Maurice is only using EasyPay, so the decline in volume is not due to using a competitor; they simply have not had the business\.
